title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry to be re-evaluated in 2 weeks after MRI reveals oblique abdominal tear
content:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry will be re-evaluated in two weeks after an MRI revealed an oblique abdominal tear suffered early against the Houston Rockets, the team announced Thursday.

Warriors coach Steve Kerr said after the game that he wasn’t sure exactly when Curry’s injury occurred. The play that drew considerable attention and speculation on social media occurred early in the first quarter. Rockets center Alperen Şengün grabbed and twisted Curry’s arm as he tried to get around a screen that Curry was setting for Draymond Green.

Curry, 38, immediately winced in pain and grabbed at his side. He played a few more minutes, even hitting a 3-pointer, before leaving in visible pain. He signaled to the Warriors’ bench and left the game at the next timeout.

The team later ruled him out for the remainder of the game. Curry left the arena for an MRI, according to Kerr. With Curry contributing just six minutes and three points, Golden State (8-4) had its eight-game winning streak snapped.

“He said he tweaked something in his abdominal area and said he’s never done it before,” Kerr said.

Kerr added that he was very concerned, before saying he didn’t yet know the extent of the injury. His star point guard missed 39 games last season because of runner’s knee and a right knee bone bruise. The Warriors went 13-26 in those games.

Curry has averaged 27.8 points per game this season through 12 games, though he has appeared in just 10 contests. Golden State is tied with the Oklahoma City Thunder for sixth in the Western Conference standings. Curry has averaged just 26.3 minutes per game in the early stages of his 18th NBA season.

Several Warriors players noted that Curry spoke to the team at halftime of Thursday’s game and wanted them to know he was OK.

“He just said, ‘I’ll be all right,’” Green said.
